review_type: source-grounded AI review; not physician adjudication
reviewed_components: all clinical facts and measured quantities
corrections: p1 testosterone level "low-normal physiological male range": flag set to normal (within the normal male range; source does not call it low); literal text_value kept.

p1 clinic visit ("1.5 years after his diagnosis of POTS") split from the gender dysphoria diagnosis and testosterone start, which the source dates only as 2 years before November 2018; relations rebuilt from the November 2018 sentence (diagnosis 4 years / testosterone 2 years before) and from both stated times of the same anchor.
p1 subsequent testosterone levels moved out of the metoprolol event into their own test event, ordered after testosterone start by the adjacent "Subsequent".

p2 February 2019 clinic visit split from the gender dysphoria diagnosis and testosterone start ("He was subsequently diagnosed"); removed the unsupported testosterone-start before March 2019 order; kept visit before March 2019 (calendar).
p2 menarche made its own history event ordered before dizziness onset ("symptom onset after menarche").

p2 trazodone split into the diagnosis medication-list item and a separate "improved with trazodone" item (consistent with the separate Strattera and atomoxetine items); added improvement outcomes for cognitive dysfunction with Strattera and insomnia with trazodone.
p2 cyproheptadine and pyridostigmine "continued" at the March 2019 visit split from the initial treatment items into separate administered items in the March 2019 event.
p2 "no other significant clinical findings" changed from an absent sign to a scoped normal-examination sign (present, literal text_value) per SECTION-SIGNS.
p2 pyridostigmine dose increase/reduction and p3 desmopressin increase: drug name kept as written, invented regimen labels replaced by literal dose_text; no dose values added.
p3 desmopressin increase and midodrine addition ("required ... subsequent addition") set to action unknown per the "required" ruling; midodrine/desmopressin use in March 2019 kept administered.

p3 desmopressin start item no longer carries the increase evidence; added order e06 -> e07 ("With regular exercise, symptoms improved. Stimulant therapy was subsequently discontinued in 2016.") and diagnosis (July 2015) -> stimulant stop (2016).

Added review_only (ambiguous) documented_sex for each patient: the pronoun "he" reflects gender identity for natal females identifying as male (precedent PMC9977334.1); sex assigned at birth and gender identity kept as accepted items.

Added review_only outcome to each patient for the explicit all-three discussion sentence "Before initiation of hormone therapy ... all three patients showed variable control, with overall improvement after addition of these interventions" ("these interventions" refers to general typical therapy).
Past-medical-history conditions given temporality historical; species_as_documented changed from a sex/gender phrase to "patient".
unresolved: Retrospective case series of three patients; no figures, tables or supplements.
Symptom severity was not objectively measured per the authors; all symptomatology was subjective.

Conclusion-section statements that are series-level or unlabelled (reduction in medication need, patients who missed testosterone) are not copied to individuals except the explicit "All three patients" improvement sentence.
Several blood pressure and heart rate values are printed without units; none were added.
Times are given as months or years only; some events (testosterone start, metoprolol treatment) have no stated date.

key_findings: Three transgender (natal female identifying as male) adolescents with POTS; each case paragraph pair (b00008-b00013) owned by one patient; no figures, tables or supplements.

The explicit "All three patients demonstrated apparent clinical improvement" sentence is correctly copied to each patient; unlabelled discussion sentences (reduction in medication need, "one of our patients" missing testosterone) are not copied.
Clinic-visit times in p1 and p2 do not govern the testosterone start; events split accordingly.
Strattera is the brand of atomoxetine but the two names occur in separate statements; kept as separate items with an ambiguity rather than merged.
Physical therapy referral recorded as a completed referral action (the referral was made), consistent with corpus precedent; attendance not claimed.
Blood pressures kept as text_value with unit only where printed.
residual_risks: Several treatment and follow-up items have deliberately null times (metoprolol, continued pain, dose changes, testosterone start in p1/p2).
documented_sex left review_only; downstream filters relying on documented_sex will see only sex assigned at birth and gender identity.
Clinical improvement statements are subjective per the authors; no objective severity measure.
